famous.title: The Game of the Century
famous.note: 13-year-old Bobby Fischer sacrifices his queen against Donald Byrne and hunts down the king with his minor pieces.

famous.title: The Opera Game
famous.note: Played in a box at the Paris opera. Morphy develops fast, sacrifices, and finishes with a textbook mating attack.

famous.title: Kasparov's Immortal
famous.note: Kasparov gives up a rook with 24.Rxd4 and chases Topalov’s king across the board in one of the deepest combinations ever played.

famous.title: Fischer vs Spassky, 1972 Game 6
famous.note: Fischer opens 1.c4 for a rare Queen’s Gambit and plays so smoothly that Spassky applauds at the end.

famous.title: Capablanca vs Marshall, 1918
famous.note: Marshall unveils his prepared gambit, the Marshall Attack. Capablanca defends calmly and wins.

famous.title: Karpov vs Kasparov, 1985 Game 16
famous.note: Kasparov’s knight on d3 paralyses White. A key win on his way to becoming world champion.

famous.title: Carlsen vs Ernst, 2004
famous.note: A 13-year-old Magnus Carlsen sacrifices his way to a mating attack at Wijk aan Zee.

famous.title: Aronian vs Anand, 2013
famous.note: Anand, with Black, launches a stunning series of sacrifices. Often called the best game of his career.

famous.title: Ding vs Gukesh, 2024 Game 14
famous.note: The last classical game of the 2024 World Championship. Heading for a draw, Ding blunders with 55.Rf2 and Gukesh becomes the youngest world champion.

famous.title: R. Byrne vs Fischer, 1963
famous.note: Fischer sacrifices with 15...Nxf2 in the US Championship. Byrne resigned while commentators still thought White was fine.

famous.title: Paulsen vs Morphy, 1857
famous.note: Morphy gives up his queen with 17...Qxf3 for a crushing attack at the First American Chess Congress.

famous.title: Botvinnik vs Tal, 1960 Game 6
famous.note: Tal’s knight sacrifice 21...Nf4 throws the world champion into chaos. Tal went on to win the title.

famous.title: Tal vs Larsen, 1965
famous.note: The deciding game of their Candidates match. Tal’s speculative 16.Nd5 sacrifice is one of the most debated moves in chess history.

famous.title: Capablanca vs Tartakower, 1924
famous.note: A classic rook endgame: Capablanca gives up pawns so his king can march in. Still taught as a model of endgame technique.

famous.title: Karpov vs Kasparov, 1985 Game 24
famous.note: The last game of the 1985 match. Kasparov wins with Black and becomes the youngest world champion at the time.

famous.title: Topalov vs Anand, 2010 Game 12
famous.note: The final game of the 2010 World Championship. Anand wins with Black to keep his title.

famous.title: Carlsen vs Anand, 2013 Game 5
famous.note: Carlsen’s first win in his World Championship match against Anand, grinding out a long endgame. He won the title a few games later.

famous.title: Carlsen vs Karjakin, 2016 Tiebreak
famous.note: The last tiebreak game of the 2016 World Championship ends with the queen sacrifice 50.Qh6+. Carlsen keeps his title.

famous.title: Carlsen vs Caruana, 2014
famous.note: Part of Caruana’s famous 7-0 start at the 2014 Sinquefield Cup, one of the greatest tournament runs ever.

famous.title: Nepomniachtchi vs Ding, 2023 Tiebreak
famous.note: The final rapid tiebreak game of the 2023 World Championship. Ding wins with Black and becomes China’s first men’s world champion.

famous.title: Gukesh vs Ding, 2024 Game 3
famous.note: After losing the first game, Gukesh strikes back for his first World Championship win to level the match.
